title: Apple and rhubarb compote with honeyed seeds

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Apples, rhubarb, an orange, honey, seeds, Greek yoghurt and two ground spices are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every item, including forced rhubarb in March and bags of pumpkin and sunflower seeds, is an everyday Tesco purchase.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, a frying pan, a knife and a zester or grater, and simmering fruit is beginner technique.

works.reason: Four apples and 400g rhubarb softened with orange juice and honey over 500g yoghurt makes a sensible breakfast for four, with clear timings and a sensible amount of water.

honest_times.reason: Coring four apples, zesting and juicing an orange and cutting rhubarb fits 15 minutes, and 5 plus 5 to 8 minutes of simmering, with the seeds toasted alongside, matches the 15-minute cook time.

honest_ingredients.reason: Each name matches its id, and every listed ingredient and spice is used in the steps with nothing extra brought in.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm apple compote with the first forced rhubarb suits late March, and the apples lead the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit, Greek yoghurt and seeds with only a little honey make a filling, real-food breakfast a family would happily eat again.
